title: Comparisons of Three Nighttime Sap Flux Density Models
content:
ABSTRACT

Sap flux density can be used as a surrogate of plants' transpiration rate; thus, measurements of sap flux density and the corresponding modelling efforts greatly improved our understanding of ecosystem transpiration. This study measured sap flux density every 10 min for three representative tree species (eight oak, Quercus variabilis; four poplar, Populus adenopoda; four pine, Pinus massoniana) of a subtropical forest ecosystem in the Hanjiang River Basin from January 2021 to December 2023. The responses of nighttime sap flux density to major environmental factors were then analysed. Vapour pressure deficit (VPD) is the most important driving factor of nighttime sap flux density for all the three tree species, explaining 12%, 27% and 51% of the variation for pine, oak and poplar, respectively; temperature (Ta) and relative humidity (RH) can explain up to 29% of the variation; soil water content (SWC) showed relatively weaker control and explained up to 14% of the variation. Then three nighttime sap flux density models were compared in this study: regression, exponential and distribution models. In particular, the regression model was established using the stepwise multiple linear regression method based on the environmental responses of nighttime sap flux density; the exponential model was proposed using an exponential decay curve by assuming the continuity of nighttime sap flux density series; the distribution model was built on the positive relationship between accumulative nighttime sap flux and daytime sap flux. The regression model can explain 12%–70% of the variation in nighttime sap flux density, the distribution model can explain 22%–72%, and the exponential model can explain −82% to 62%. When evaluating the three models using root mean square error (RMSE) and the Akaike information criterion (AIC), the distribution model performed the best with the lowest RMSE and AIC. The findings advance our understanding of tree transpiration of this region and lay a foundation for modelling efforts of nighttime sap flux density.
